clue.text: Showing initiative, break in using a jemmy

parts.note: to break in is to force an entry, to enter a building
a jemmy is a burglar's crowbar, used for prising doors and windows open

explanation.surface: A burglar is admired for his resourcefulness in breaking into a house with a crowbar.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone enterprising is resourceful and bold, the very quality of taking initiative.

clue.text: For instance, a former partner has plenty

parts.note: an ex is a former partner or spouse
ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: An ex-spouse, for instance, is said to be very well off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' and 'a' and 'has' are link words; the definition is 'instance', as in 'for instance'.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a case illustrating a point, a synonym for a specimen or illustration.

clue.text: Handful of notes could provide travel permit

parts.note: a trip is a journey, travel
to let is to permit or allow

explanation.surface: Some banknotes might buy a travel permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' looks like money, but they are musical: three notes played in the time of two.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of three notes played in the time of two is a small musical group, a handful.

clue.text: Well off now

parts.note: right can mean well, as in feeling all right
away means off, not here

explanation.surface: Someone who is wealthy at the present moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well off' reads as rich; split it into 'Well' and 'off'.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something immediately is to do it at once, without delay.

clue.text: Severely criticise emperor holding nothing up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters are read from bottom to top
holding means the emperor contains the nothing inside him

parts.note: a tsar was a Russian emperor
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A ruler is harshly attacked while keeping nothing back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts O into TSAR, giving TSAOR, and 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan someone savagely, as critics do, is to give them a scathing attack.

clue.text: An officer of the crown, the lady repeated phrases

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman, the lady
a riff is a repeated musical phrase

explanation.surface: A royal official, a woman, keeps repeating herself.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer appointed by the Crown to keep the peace and administer a county or shire.

clue.text: Garment for a woman, almost one for a man

parts.note: nigh means nearly, almost
a tie is a garment for a man, worn round the neck

explanation.surface: A woman's item of clothing that is almost like a man's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'Garment': a garment for a man is a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of nightdress, worn to bed by women and girls.

clue.text: Moving critter to ark -— an American custom

indicators.note: Moving shows the letters of the following words are shifted into new places

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Noah loading an animal onto the ark, described as a quaint New World tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'critter', American slang for creature, adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween door-to-door begging by children in costume is a custom from the United States.

clue.text: Passage in town

definitions.meaning: a passage read aloud from a text, as a lesson in church
the Berkshire town west of London

explanation.walkthrough: The Berkshire town is a large commuter town west of London on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson read from scripture is called by this name, and it is also a well-known English town.

clue.text: Got back at Geneva, changed, then departs

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of Geneva are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder
D is the abbreviation for departs, as on a timetable

explanation.surface: Someone returned at Geneva, switched trains, and set off again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got back at' looks like arriving home at Geneva, but it is the definition, meaning took revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: To get back at someone is to take revenge, a close synonym for exacting retribution.

clue.text: Horror when father goes round about island dropping ring

indicators.note: goes round means father encloses the word for about

parts.note: dad is a word for father
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: dropping says the round letter falls out of the island's name

parts.note: Foulness is an island off the Essex coast
O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: A man is appalled as his father circles an island but loses a ring overboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Foulness is a low-lying island off the coast of Essex, England; the parse removes its ring-shaped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Horror and dreadfulness are both the quality of being terrible or appalling.

clue.text: Get into trouble — look inside for crew member

indicators.note: inside means the word for look is placed within the phrase for getting into trouble

parts.note: to cop it is British slang for getting into trouble or being punished
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A warning that someone will be in trouble if they peek indoors, to find a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cop it' is British slang for getting into trouble or being punished.
explanation.definitionFit: A second pilot on an aircraft is one of the flight crew.

clue.text: Emblem shifted in the list

indicators.note: shifted indicates that the letters of the next words are moved around

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a badge has been moved to a different place on a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifted' rearranges THE LIST; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: This prickly plant is the national emblem of Scotland.

clue.text: Public upset after vase is lost

indicators.note: is lost says the word for vase disappears from the longer word

parts.note: to upset is to overturn, knock over
an urn is a vase-shaped container

explanation.surface: Someone is openly distressed after a vase has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the emotion but means knocked over; 'after' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in public is done openly, in plain view rather than hidden.

clue.text: Primrose can be seen here from track adjoining meadow

parts.note: a wake is the track left in water by a ship
a field is a meadow or pasture

explanation.surface: A primrose flower might be spotted along a path running beside a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Primrose is the title character of Goldsmith's novel The Vicar of Wakefield, so he is found in that Yorkshire town; the surface suggests the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Goldsmith's clergyman Dr Primrose is the vicar of this West Yorkshire town in his famous novel.

clue.text: Commotion at end of trick feel ruff is mistaken

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word trick
is mistaken indicates the letters are set down wrongly, in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A card player is wrong to sense a trump at the last trick, causing a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: A ruff in bridge or whist is playing a trump on a trick, which fits the card-table picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss or disturbance, a noisy to-do, is a commotion.

clue.text: We may sort out Finn's friend

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the preceding words are put into disorder

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An offer to help get one's friend Finn's affairs in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort out' reads as a phrase but 'sort' is fodder; 'out' alone rearranges WE MAY SORT. Huckleberry Finn's friend is Mark Twain's boy hero.
explanation.definitionFit: In Mark Twain's novels this boy is the best friend of Huckleberry Finn.

clue.text: Piece of jewellery stuck under low berth

indicators.note: stuck under places the jewellery below the low sound in this down answer

parts.note: to low is to moo, as a cow does
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: A brooch got wedged beneath a low bunk on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the verb for a cow's call, not the opposite of high.
explanation.definitionFit: A berth is a place where a ship is tied up, a mooring.

clue.text: Disembarks when traffic control is introduced

indicators.note: is introduced means the traffic control is put inside the word for when

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
traffic lights control the flow of traffic

explanation.surface: Passengers get off once a new system of traffic control is brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: To get down from a bus or train is to step off it, to leave the vehicle.

clue.text: Island where copper caught a disease of sheep

indicators.note: caught means the copper symbol holds the sheep disease within it

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
orf is a viral skin disease of sheep and goats

explanation.surface: A tale of a policeman on a holiday island picking up a livestock ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but is the element, Cu; 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: This Greek island lies in the Ionian Sea off the coast of Albania.

clue.text: Letter revealing opposition to wine

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
anti means against, opposition

explanation.surface: A letter reveals someone's objection to drinking wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A red wine from the Tuscany region of Italy.

clue.text: Search vigorously over time for small part of plant

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the search word on top of the letter for time

parts.note: to rootle is to rummage or search about, like a pig

explanation.surface: Someone digs energetically for a long while to find a tiny plant fragment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Search vigorously' suggests ROOT, but here it is the British ROOTLE, to rummage about.
explanation.definitionFit: A small subsidiary root growing from a larger one is a minor part of a plant.

clue.text: Controversial end to coffee grounds

indicators.note: end to picks out the final letter of the word coffee

parts.note: grounds for doing something are its motive or reason

explanation.surface: A heated argument about stopping coffee grounds being thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coffee grounds' reads as one thing, but 'grounds' means reasons.
explanation.definitionFit: A controversial issue stirs strong feelings, and arousing feeling is what an emotive topic does.

clue.text: Jane guards one elevated stronghold

indicators.note: guards means Jane surrounds the numeral for one

parts.note: Jane Eyre is the heroine of Charlotte Bronte's novel
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A woman named Jane keeps watch over a hilltop fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey's nest built high on a crag is a lofty refuge, an elevated stronghold.

clue.text: Creature supplying educational establishment with food

parts.note: uni is the short form of university
corn is grain, food for people and animals

explanation.surface: An animal is fed by a college that provides it with grain.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horned horse of legend is a mythical beast, a creature of fable.

clue.text: Some get hit hereabouts, in that direction

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A warning that some people around here are likely to be struck.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned adverb meaning to or towards that place, the opposite of hither.

clue.text: Ends with several drinks after a bit of fish

indicators.note: after places the drinks behind the piece of fish in the answer

parts.note: a fin is part of a fish
ales are beers, several drinks

explanation.surface: A meal ends with a round of beers after a little fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of fish' suggests a single letter F, but it is a whole part of the fish, a FIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing sections of shows or pieces of music are their concluding ends.

clue.text: Encourages little boy with order for this dish

parts.note: to egg on is to encourage
Ben is a boy's name, short for Benjamin
an edict is an official order or decree

explanation.surface: A parent spurs on a small son while ordering a breakfast dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Poached eggs on muffins with ham and hollandaise sauce make a classic brunch dish.
